C01.d: The process of linking the local system of a model or drawing to a known terrestrial reference system, so that every point in the model has unambiguous real-world coordinates (E, N, H).
C01.ej: A building model in Madrid expressed in ETRS89 / UTM zone 30N (EPSG:25830), with heights above mean sea level at Alicante.
C01.eq: Revit: shared coordinates; Archicad/Allplan/Vectorworks: Survey Point; Tekla: base point; Bentley: GCS; IFC: IfcMapConversion + IfcProjectedCRS.
C01.err: Believing that entering latitude/longitude in the project location amounts to georeferencing; that only places the project approximately.

C02.d: The combination of a datum (how it is anchored to the Earth) and a coordinate system (geographic, projected or vertical) that allows positions to be expressed unambiguously.
C02.ej: ETRS89 / UTM zone 30N (EPSG:25830) for horizontal position + Alicante height (EPSG:5782) for heights; together they form a compound CRS.
C02.eq: Civil 3D: coordinate system zone (GEOCSASSIGN); Bentley: GCS; ArcGIS/QGIS: CRS; IFC: IfcProjectedCRS / IfcGeographicCRS.
C02.err: Stating only 'UTM 30' without the datum: ED50 and ETRS89 in UTM zone 30 differ by about 200 m in Spain.

C03.d: A mathematical model (ellipsoid + orientation and origin) that fixes how coordinates relate to the real Earth. Changing the datum moves the coordinates even though the physical point is the same.
C03.ej: Official on the Iberian Peninsula and the Balearic Islands: ETRS89 (GRS80 ellipsoid); Canary Islands: REGCAN95; historical: ED50 (International 1924 ellipsoid). WGS84 is the GPS datum. Without an epoch it is ambiguous: it drifts away from ETRS89 by about 2.5 cm a year because of the motion of the Eurasian plate, and today the difference is tens of centimetres.
C03.eq: Chosen when the CRS is defined: Civil 3D, Bentley GCS, IfcProjectedCRS.GeodeticDatum.
C03.err: Mixing old ED50 mapping with ETRS89 GNSS surveys without transforming them (offsets of ~150-230 m).

C04.d: A numerical identifier from the EPSG registry (IOGP) that uniquely defines a CRS, datum or transformation. WKT (ISO 19162) is the text-based alternative that fully describes the CRS.
C04.ej: EPSG:25829, 25830, 25831 (ETRS89 / UTM zones 29N, 30N, 31N); EPSG:4083 and 4082 (REGCAN95 / UTM zones 28N and 27N); EPSG:5782 (Alicante heights).
C04.eq: Revit (IFC exporter): EPSG field; Civil 3D: GEOCSASSIGN accepts EPSG codes; IFC: IfcProjectedCRS.Name = 'EPSG:25830'; IFC4.3: IfcWellKnownText.
C04.err: Writing the name of the system without a code, using a code from another datum (23030 is ED50 / UTM zone 30N) or one with a different axis order (3042 is ETRS89 / UTM zone 30N in North-East order).

C05.d: A mathematical transformation from geographic coordinates (latitude, longitude) to a plane (Easting, Northing). UTM divides the Earth into 6° zones with a scale factor of 0.9996 on the central meridian.
C05.ej: Mainland Spain uses zones 29, 30 and 31; the Canary Islands, 27 and 28. A project stays in a single zone even when it is close to the boundary.
C05.eq: A CRS parameter in every program; IFC: IfcProjectedCRS.MapProjection and MapZone.
C05.err: Switching zones within the same project or getting the Canary Islands zone wrong.

C06.t: Local site coordinates vs projected coordinates
C06.d: Local coordinates have an origin and orientation convenient for the site and measure 'as with a tape'; projected coordinates (e.g. UTM) are large numbers and carry the distortion of the projection. A low distortion projection (LDP) is a projection designed so that the scale is ~1 on the site.
C06.ej: A small project (≤100 m) in local coordinates with two or more tie points to UTM. For a long linear project, UTM with a managed scale factor or an LDP: Deutsche Bahn brought distortion below 5 ppm at 6 326 stations (Clemen and Romanschek, ISPRS 2025).
C06.eq: Revit: Project Base Point vs Survey Point; Tekla: base points; Trimble/Leica: site calibration.
C06.err: Modelling in real UTM coordinates inside the BIM program (loss of precision) instead of modelling locally and transforming.

C07.t: Ellipsoidal height, orthometric height, geoid, vertical datum
C07.d: Ellipsoidal height (h) is given by GNSS relative to the ellipsoid; orthometric height (H) is the 'height above sea level' relative to the geoid. They are related by the geoid undulation: N = h − H. The vertical datum defines the zero for heights.
C07.ej: In Spain, H is referred to mean sea level at Alicante (REDNAP network); the IGN publishes the EGM08-REDNAP geoid (~3.8 cm accuracy). In the Canary Islands each island has its own reference.
C07.eq: Revit: Survey Point elevation; IFC: IfcMapConversion.OrthogonalHeight and IfcProjectedCRS.VerticalDatum.
C07.err: Giving the model ellipsoidal heights from a GNSS receiver as if they were levels (errors of ~50 m on the Peninsula).

C08.t: Scale factor (grid, elevation, combined) / grid vs ground
C08.d: The distance measured on the ground does not match the distance on the UTM grid. The grid scale factor depends on the position within the zone; the elevation factor, on the height above the ellipsoid; the combined scale factor is their product. You have to decide whether to model 'at ground' or 'at grid'.
C08.ej: Typical differences of 100 to 400 ppm in Spain: 1 to 4 cm every 100 m. The 2024 road technical note Nota de Servicio 03/2024 requires the survey to state the grid distortion coefficient (K) and the convergence (W).
C08.eq: Civil 3D: Grid Scale Factor (Transformation); IFC: IfcMapConversion.Scale (units) and IfcMapConversionScaled (IFC4.3, FactorX/Y/Z); Trimble/Leica: calibration. Revit: does not handle it (a BEP decision).
C08.err: Confusing the two uses of IfcMapConversion.Scale: the 2020 bSI guide, OSArch and Bonsai use it as the combined scale factor, whereas IFC 4.3 ADD2 reserves it for unit conversion and moves the grid scale factor to IfcMapConversionScaled. Ignoring the factor on long linear projects is also a mistake.

C09.t: True north, grid north, magnetic north, project north
C09.d: True (geographic) north: towards the pole. Grid north: the N axis of the projection (UTM). Magnetic north: the compass north. Project north: the 'up' direction of the model, aligned with the building grid for convenient working.
C09.ej: In Spain the difference between true north and UTM grid north (grid convergence) can exceed 2° at the zone edges.
C09.eq: Revit: Project North / True North; Archicad: Project North; Tekla: angle to North; IFC: TrueNorth and the IfcMapConversion rotation (relative to grid north).
C09.err: Entering the angle relative to the UTM grid as the 'angle to true north' without noticing, or the other way round.

C10.d: The angle between true north and grid north at a point. In BIM, the rotation angle of the local→world transformation must state which north it is measured from and in which direction of rotation.
C10.ej: Zero on the central meridian of the zone (3°W for zone 30) and increasing towards the edges.
C10.eq: Revit: angle measured clockwise; Archicad: anticlockwise from +X; IFC: XAxisAbscissa / XAxisOrdinate (anticlockwise from East).
C10.err: Mixing rotation conventions between programs (Revit vs Archicad) and ending up with a rotated model.

C11.d: The fixed 0,0,0 point of the program's geometry engine, to which all internal coordinates refer. It does not move; geometry should be modelled close to it.
C11.ej: In Revit it has been visible since version 2020.2.
C11.eq: Revit: Internal Origin; Archicad: Project Origin; Tekla: model origin; Allplan: global 0,0,0 point; Vectorworks: Internal Origin; BricsCAD: WCS 0,0,0; Bonsai/IFC: local origin.
C11.err: Importing a DWG in UTM 'origin to origin': the geometry ends up kilometres away from the internal origin.

C12.d: The local reference of the project, usually at a corner or a grid intersection, used for dimensioning and setting out in building coordinates. It is not the link to the real world.
C12.ej: The intersection of grid lines A-1 of a structure.
C12.eq: Revit: Project Base Point; Tekla: project base point; Allplan 2026: Base Point; Vectorworks: User Origin; BricsCAD: Project Location; IFC: placement of IfcSite/IfcBuilding.
C12.err: Moving the base point in the belief that this georeferences the model.

C13.d: Marker that shows coordinates of the shared or survey system. Clipped, it sits at the origin of that system and moving it relocates the system relative to the model; unclipped, it is moved to a known point (a setting-out control point) without changing anything, only to read or check coordinates.
C13.ej: Unclipped, placed on a setting-out control point with known ETRS89 / UTM 30N coordinates to check that the model reads them correctly.
C13.eq: Revit: Survey Point (clipped or unclipped); Archicad (AC25+): Survey Point; Allplan 2026 and Vectorworks: Survey Point; BricsCAD: Survey Location; Tekla: base point with E/N; IFC: IfcMapConversion.
C13.err: Moving the point while clipped when you meant unclipped (or vice versa), shifting the whole shared coordinate system.

C14.d: The mechanism by which several linked models use the same coordinate system. You acquire the system of another model or publish your own to it; named sites (locations) allow several positions of the same model.
C14.ej: A master site model that acquires from the survey model and publishes to the architecture, structure and MEP models.
C14.eq: Revit: Acquire Coordinates/Publish Coordinates, shared site (named location), Relocate Project, Reset Shared Coordinates; ACC: acquire only under cloud worksharing; other programs: the same logic with their Survey Point.
C14.err: Confusing 'being at the same coordinates' with 'sharing coordinates'; using Publish Coordinates with a DWG.

C15.t: Floating-point precision / large coordinates / false origin
C15.d: Graphics engines store coordinates with a limited number of significant digits: far from the origin, precision is lost, geometry 'jitters' and errors appear. That is why you model close to the origin and apply a transformation (false origin).
C15.ej: Revit limits geometry to 16 km (10 miles) from the internal origin; Bonsai warns of millimetre errors from about 5 km.
C15.eq: Revit: distance limit; Bonsai: False Origin; Navisworks/Solibri: flickering with large coordinates; Bentley: Global Origin.
C15.err: Modelling directly in UTM coordinates (400000, 4400000) inside the BIM program.

C16.d: An operation that converts coordinates from one system to another: from local to projected (translation + rotation + scale, Helmert 2D/3D type) or between datums (e.g. ED50→ETRS89 using the IGN NTv2 grid).
C16.ej: NTv2 grids: PENR2009 and BALR2009 from the IGN (a few cm), SPED2ETV2 from the EPSG registry (EPSG:15932, 0.1-0.2 m) and the ICGC grid for Catalonia (EPSG:5661). It is worth checking which one each program uses.
C16.eq: IFC: IfcMapConversion (local→projected); CloudCompare: Global Shift; FME/PROJ/QGIS: reprojection; Civil 3D: library transformations.
C16.err: Applying rotation and translation in the wrong order (in Modelical's point cloud workflow you translate first and then rotate).

C17.d: Combining models from different disciplines and programs in a common viewer to coordinate them (clash detection, review). It only works if they all share the same coordinate system.
C17.ej: Architecture (Archicad), structure (Tekla) and MEP (Revit) models federated in Navisworks or BIMcollab.
C17.eq: Navisworks: Units and Transform; ACC: Transform; BIMcollab Zoom: IFC Global Origin / Use georeferencing; Solibri; Trimble Connect; Dalux.
C17.err: Using the viewer's Transform as a permanent fix instead of correcting the origin in the source model.

C18.d: Attributes of the IFC site that give an approximate position in WGS84 (degrees, minutes, seconds) and an elevation. They are informative: they do not define a precise transformation.
C18.ej: Latitude 40°25'N, longitude 3°42'W for a project in Madrid.
C18.eq: Revit: project location (map); Archicad: Project Location; all IFC exporters.
C18.err: Taking the IfcSite lat/long as precise georeferencing, or leaving them at 0 (common according to TU Delft).

C19.d: An IFC entity (since IFC4) that defines the transformation from the model's local system to the map CRS: Eastings, Northings, OrthogonalHeight, rotation (XAxisAbscissa/Ordinate) and scale. IFC4.3 adds IfcMapConversionScaled (FactorX/Y/Z) and IfcRigidOperation (translation only).
C19.eq: Revit (IFC4 with EPSG), Archicad (Survey Point and Project Origin), Tekla (IfcMapConversion option), Vectorworks, Bonsai, Allplan; in IFC2x3 it is emulated with ePSet_MapConversion.
C19.err: Double offset: coordinates written both in IfcMapConversion and in the IfcSite placement.

C20.d: The IFC entity that identifies the target CRS of IfcMapConversion: name (EPSG code), geodetic datum, vertical datum, projection, zone and units. In IFC4.3 the CRS must carry an EPSG code or a WKT.
C20.ej: Name 'EPSG:25830', GeodeticDatum 'EPSG:6258' (ETRS89), VerticalDatum referred to Alicante, MapZone '30N'.
C20.eq: EPSG field in the IFC exporter of Revit, Archicad, Vectorworks, Bonsai; IFC2x3: ePSet_ProjectedCRS.
C20.err: Leaving the name empty or filled with free text that viewers cannot interpret.

C21.d: The representation context of the IFC project, which contains the world coordinate system and the direction of true north. If IfcMapConversion is present, TrueNorth is informative only.
C21.ej: TrueNorth rotated 12° from the model's Y axis.
C21.eq: Revit 'Coordinate Base' with 'oriented in True North' variants; all exporters.
C21.err: TrueNorth inconsistent with the IfcMapConversion rotation.

C22.d: A classification (HTW Dresden) of how complete the georeferencing of an IFC file is: 10 postal address, 20 lat/long in IfcSite, 30 placement of the top-level element, 40 WorldCoordinateSystem + TrueNorth, 50 IfcMapConversion + IfcProjectedCRS (recommended).
C22.ej: Require LoGeoRef 50 in the BEP and check it with IfcGeoRefChecker, IfcGref or IDS.
C22.eq: IfcGeoRefChecker, IfcGref (TU Delft), Bonsai, IDS validators, BIM Fit Check (buildingSMART Germany).
C22.err: Accepting as valid an IFC file that only reaches LoGeoRef 20 (lat/long).

C23.d: IFC 4.3 (ISO 16739-1:2024) adds roads, railways, bridges and ports, with alignments (horizontal, vertical, cant) and linear referencing (chainage / stationing) as well as new georeferencing entities.
C23.ej: A motorway main line from chainage 0+000 to 12+500 georeferenced in EPSG:25830.
C23.eq: Civil 3D, OpenRoads/OpenRail, Istram, Allplan Civil, Bonsai.
C23.err: Exporting a linear project to generic IFC4 and losing the alignment and chainage.

C24.d: The settings of each program's IFC exporter/importer that decide which origin is written (internal, project base point, survey point, shared) and whether IfcMapConversion/IfcProjectedCRS or IFC2x3 property sets are generated.
C24.ej: Revit: Coordinate Base = Shared Coordinates + EPSG in IFC4; Archicad: Survey Point and Project Origin; Tekla: IfcMapConversion or IfcSite.
C24.eq: Revit IFC exporter (6 Coordinate Base options); Archicad translators; Tekla IFC export; Vectorworks; Allplan; CYPE; BricsCAD.
C24.err: Mixing IFC files exported with different settings in the same viewer.

C25.d: An agreement documented in the exchange information requirements (EIR) and the BIM execution plan (BEP) that fixes the CRS, vertical datum, control points, rotation, units, scale factor, who is responsible for the site model and how to export.
C25.ej: The es.BIM guide asks for a 'project coordination base point' georeferenced in X, Y, Z, outside the building and with positive coordinates, and at least two documented points. ETS (Basque Country, 2024) specifies ETRS89 (ETRF2000, epoch 2017.0), UTM zone 30 and the EGM08-REDNAP geoid.
C25.eq: Software-independent; applied in each program through its equivalent Survey Point.
C25.err: Not agreeing on it at the start and discovering the offset at the first federation.

C26.d: Laser or photogrammetric scans registered in a real-world coordinate system. Because of their large coordinates, they usually need a global shift before they go into the BIM program.
C26.ej: ReCap → Dynamo → CloudCompare (Global Shift) → ReCap → Revit origin-to-origin workflow (Modelical).
C26.eq: ReCap, CloudCompare (Global Shift), Trimble RealWorks, Leica Cyclone; in Revit, origin-to-origin insertion or by shared coordinates.
C26.err: 'Jittering points' when inserting a point cloud in UTM without a shift.

C27.d: Fieldwork that measures the terrain and sets out the design on site. It requires setting-out control points with known coordinates and a calibration that relates the site system to GNSS.
C27.ej: A network of setting-out control points tied to the IGN ERGNSS/REGENTE network.
C27.eq: Trimble Business Center/Siteworks, Leica Infinity/Captivate (site calibration), Civil 3D, Istram, TcpMDT.
C27.err: Setting out with coordinates from a model that did not share the surveyor's system.

C28.d: The combined use of BIM models and geospatial data (mapping, 3D city models) in the same environment, which requires the BIM model to be properly georeferenced and in the correct CRS.
C28.ej: The project IFC model loaded over IGN mapping or a municipal CityGML model.
C28.eq: ArcGIS GeoBIM / ArcGIS Pro, QGIS, FME, Cesium (3D Tiles), Autodesk Forma, Bentley iTwin.
C28.err: Taking an IFC file without IfcMapConversion into GIS: it appears in the ocean off Ghana (0,0).

C29.d: The approximate position of the project (address or lat/long) used for sun studies, climate or map context. It does not replace shared coordinates.
C29.ej: Location by postal address in Revit or Forma for solar studies.
C29.eq: Revit: Location (Internet Mapping Service); Archicad: Project Location; Forma; IfcSite lat/long; IfcPostalAddress.
C29.err: Thinking that geolocating on the map already puts the model in the correct UTM coordinates.

C30.d: Common data environments (ACC/BIM 360, Trimble Connect, Bentley iTwin, Dalux, BIMcollab Cloud, usBIM) where models are shared and federated; each has its own rules about coordinates and transformations.
C30.ej: In ACC with cloud worksharing, Publish Coordinates may be disabled and you can only acquire from the master model.
C30.eq: ACC Model Coordination (Transform), Trimble Connect, iTwin (linear/projected geolocation), Dalux, usBIM.
C30.err: Transforming the model only in the cloud and forgetting that the original is still offset.

C31.t: CAD coordinate systems (WCS/UCS, DWG, DGN GCS, global origin)
C31.d: In CAD, geometry is drawn directly in coordinates (WCS) and the UCS is an auxiliary system. Bentley DGN files add a GCS and a Global Origin.
C31.ej: A topographic survey DWG in UTM zone 30N with a rotated UCS that causes confusion when it is linked.
C31.eq: AutoCAD/Civil 3D: WCS/UCS, GEOGRAPHICLOCATION; MicroStation: GCS, Global Origin, ACS; BricsCAD.
C31.err: Linking a DWG with additional UCSs without checking them.

C32.d: Systematic checks to detect offsets, rotations and height errors: witness objects at control points, verification in a neutral viewer, LoGeoRef check and comparison of the coordinates of known points.
C32.ej: A 1 m³ cube or a physical 'Base Point' (ETS manual of the Basque Government) at each control point.
C32.eq: Navisworks, Solibri, BIMcollab, IfcGeoRefChecker, IfcGref, Bonsai, IDS.
C32.err: Validating only visually in the authoring program.

C33.d: Royal Decree RD 1071/2007 sets ETRS89 (Peninsula and Balearic Islands) and REGCAN95 (Canary Islands) as the official systems, the UTM projection and heights referred to mean sea level at Alicante. The IGN maintains the REGENTE, REDNAP and ERGNSS networks.
C33.ej: Public project in Spain: EPSG:25830 + REDNAP heights (EPSG:5782). Order PCM/818/2023 and the IGN BIM Plan require as-built models in IFC 4.3 referred to the official geodetic system.
C33.eq: Affects the choice of CRS in every program.
C33.err: Still using ED50 on new commissions or mixing Canary Islands and Peninsula systems.

C34.d: The model units (mm, m, feet) and the CRS units (usually metres) must match; in IFC the Scale field of IfcMapConversion converts model units to map units.
C34.ej: Model in millimetres: Scale = 0.001 if the CRS is in metres.
C34.eq: Revit (project units; does not support the US survey foot), IFC Scale/MapUnit, Civil 3D (drawing units).
C34.err: Exporting IFC in mm with Scale = 1 and a CRS in metres (error documented in revit-ifc #784).

C35.t: Reference epoch / plate motion / dynamic datum
C35.d: Tectonic plates move a few centimetres a year, so the coordinates of a point in a global frame (ITRF, WGS84) change over time. A 'static' datum fixes the coordinates at a date (epoch); a dynamic datum updates them. Without stating the epoch, coordinates are not comparable to the centimetre.
C35.ej: ETRS89 is tied to the Eurasian plate and barely changes in Spain, but it drifts away from WGS84 by about 2.5 cm/year. The ETS manual specifies ETRF2000 epoch 2017.0. In Australia (GDA94→GDA2020) the jump was about 1.8 m.
C35.eq: Trimble Business Center, Leica Infinity, Civil 3D (time-dependent transformations); IFC: IfcSite lat/long in WGS84 without an epoch, which is why it is only good to the metre.
C35.err: Mixing same-day GNSS coordinates in WGS84/ITRF with ETRS89 mapping, or MGA94 data with MGA2020 in Australia (a gas pipeline 300 mm out in the Worrell case).

N01.d: Framework that defines the extent and granularity of the information required for each object: which geometrical information, alphanumerical information and documentation is needed for a purpose, at an information delivery milestone and between specific actors (ISO 7817-1).
N01.ej: A fire door at detailed design stage, to demonstrate fire safety: clear opening width and swing direction; class EI2 60-C5; test certificate.
N01.eq: Revit/Archicad: not an object in its own right; it becomes parameters, templates and an IDS. Platforms such as Cobuilder Require, BIMQ or Plannerly store it in a database.
N01.err: Treating it as a single number for the whole model (“LOIN 3 model”) or as the sum LOD + LOI.

N02.d: Part of the level of information need that describes the shape of the object through five aspects: detail, dimensionality, location, appearance and parametric behaviour.
N02.ej: Door at detailed design: low detail, 3D, absolute location, symbolic appearance, no parametric behaviour.
N02.eq: Embodied in the family geometry (Revit), the GDL object (Archicad) or the IFC representation.
N02.err: Confusing it with the view detail level (coarse, medium, fine), which only decides what is drawn at each scale.

N03.d: Part of the level of information need made up of the object's identification (name, type, code, classification) and its information content (properties with name, value, unit and allowed values).
N03.eq: Revit: (shared) parameters; Archicad: properties; Allplan: attributes; Tekla: UDAs and property sets; IFC: attributes and Psets.
N03.err: Requesting properties without a standardised name or data type: “60 min”, “EI60” and “yes” all arrive for the same question.

N04.d: Set of documents that accompany an object or delivery and are not part of the model: data sheets, certificates, photographs, manuals, shop drawings.
N04.ej: Fire resistance test certificate for the door, as a PDF, linked to the type.
N04.eq: IFC: IfcDocumentReference associated through IfcRelAssociatesDocument; in CDEs, documents linked to the element.
N04.err: Requesting “technical documentation” without saying which document, in which format and for which milestone.

N05.d: The use the information will be put to (coordinating, quantity take-off, demonstrating fire safety, maintenance...). It is the first condition for setting the level of information need.
N05.ej: Purpose “demonstrate fire safety” for the building permit.
N05.eq: IDS: purpose field in the <info> header.
N05.err: Requesting information “just in case”, with no purpose: it leads to over-modelling.

N06.d: Agreed point in time at which information is exchanged: end of a stage, tender, permit, handover. The level of information need is set for each milestone.
N06.ej: Concept design, basic design, detailed design, construction and final handover.
N06.eq: IDS: milestone field in the header; ISO 19650: delivery plan (MIDP).
N06.err: Requesting at design stage data that are only known once the contract is let (manufacturer, serial number).

N07.d: Who requests the information (appointing party: the client or the lead contractor) and who produces it (appointed party). Every requirement identifies them.
N07.ej: The client requests; the architecture team delivers the doors at detailed design and the joiner during construction.
N07.eq: Responsibility matrix in the BEP; requirements management platforms with one IDS per actor.
N07.err: Not assigning a responsible party: the data falls into no man's land between two disciplines.

N08.d: Producing more geometry or more data than any purpose needs. It costs effort to create, check and maintain, and it adds noise.
N08.ej: Modelling ironmongery and fixings for every door at concept design.
N08.eq: BIMForum 2025 strengthens its “Expansion” paragraphs to respond to requests for excessive LODs.
N08.err: Thinking a more detailed model is always better.

N09.d: Scale from 100 to 500 (plus 350) indicating how far the geometry and information of an element can be relied on. It emerged around 2004-2005 (Vico) and the AIA adopted it in E202-2008.
N09.ej: LOD 300: quantity, size, shape, location and orientation measurable in the model.
N09.eq: BIMForum LOD Specification (definitions per element); BEP element matrices.
N09.err: Applying it to the whole model (“LOD 300 model”); BIMForum: “There is no such thing as an LOD ### model”.

N10.d: How much graphical detail an element contains. BIMForum distinguishes it from development: detail is the input; development, the reliable output.
N10.ej: A catalogue door with handle and hinges drawn but no product chosen: plenty of detail, little development.
N10.eq: United Kingdom (NBS): LOD = level of detail (graphical). Not to be confused with the view detail level.
N10.err: Taking graphical detail as proof that the element has been decided.

N11.d: Level of the non-graphical (alphanumerical) information of an element. Used in the United Kingdom (NBS BIM Toolkit) and Germany (alongside LOG), now absorbed into the level of information need.
N11.ej: LOI of a door at detailed design: type, fire resistance, thermal transmittance, acoustics.
N11.eq: Germany: LOG (geometry) + LOI; Peru: matrix with LOD and LOI.
N11.err: Using LOD and LOI as two loose numbers with no purpose or milestone.

N12.d: USIBD scale (LOA10 to LOA50) that sets, at 95 % confidence, the permissible deviation of what is measured and what is represented from reality.
N12.ej: LOA30 (5-15 mm) for the survey of an existing building that is going to be refurbished.
N12.eq: Laser scanning and point clouds (ReCap, CloudCompare); guides such as Metrolinx's combine it with LOIN.
N12.err: Requesting a high LOD for an existing building model without setting the accuracy of the survey.

N13.d: International standard (2024) “Building information modelling — Level of information need — Part 1: Concepts and principles”. It supersedes EN 17412-1 with no substantive changes; in Spain, UNE-EN ISO 7817-1:2025.
N13.ej: UNE-EN ISO 7817-1:2025 supersedes UNE-EN 17412-1:2021, withdrawn on 2025-01-22.
N13.eq: BIMForum 2025 describes each LOD using the aspects of ISO 7817-1.
N13.err: Still citing UNE-EN 17412-1 in tender documents issued after 2025.

N14.d: First European standard (CEN, 2020) on the level of information need. Withdrawn and superseded by EN ISO 7817-1:2024.
N14.ej: UNE-EN 17412-1:2021, published on 2021-04-28 and withdrawn on 2025-01-22.

N15.d: ISO 19650 chain of requirements: from the organization (OIR) and the asset (AIR) to the project (PIR) and each exchange (EIR), where the level of information need is set.
N15.ej: The EIR of an architecture appointment requires the doors with their fire resistance at detailed design.
N15.eq: Requirements platforms (BIMQ, Plannerly, Cobuilder Require); IDS attached to the EIR.
N15.err: Writing the EIR with generic levels (“LOD 300”) and no purpose or milestone.

N16.t: Master / task information delivery plan (MIDP / TIDP)
N16.d: ISO 19650 plans stating which information container each team delivers, who delivers it and when. They put milestones and the level of information need into practice.
N16.ej: Structural team TIDP: structural model at LOD 350 for the detailed design milestone.
N16.eq: Spreadsheets or the planning modules of CDEs.
N16.err: Planning deliveries without linking them to the requirements of each milestone.

N17.d: Specification (since 2013, almost yearly) that defines what each LOD means for each element type, with illustrations. It added LOD 350; the 2025 edition incorporates the aspects of ISO 7817-1. There is an official Spanish version for 2024 and 2025.
N17.ej: 2025 edition in Spanish, translated with BIMForum Ecuador (February 2026).
N17.eq: Reference for element matrices in any authoring tool.
N17.err: Believing it says which LOD applies at each stage: “that determination is left to each project team”.

N18.d: Contract documents of the American Institute of Architects: E202-2008 introduced the Level of Development definitions; in 2013 they were revised in E203, G201 and G202.
N18.err: Using the 2008 E202 exhibit as if it were the current version.

N19.t: UK LOD and LOI (PAS 1192 / NBS BIM Toolkit)
N19.d: British scales of graphical (LOD) and non-graphical (LOI) level by stage. NBS considers them superseded by ISO 19650, EN 17412-1 and the level of information need.
N19.err: Mixing the British scale (1-7) with the US scale (100-500).

N20.d: ISO 23386 sets out how to describe properties and maintain interconnected dictionaries; ISO 23387 defines data templates that group the properties of each object type.
N20.ej: Fire door data template with its fire resistance class and allowed values.
N20.eq: bSDD; requirements management platforms; property import in Allplan and Archicad.
N20.err: Inventing different property names on every project.

N21.d: buildingSMART online service that publishes dictionaries of classes and properties according to ISO 23386, linked to IFC entities and with allowed values.
N21.ej: Fire resistance property with values REI30 to REI120 in a national dictionary.
N21.eq: Allplan 2026 integrates more than 300 dictionaries; Bonsai 0.8.5 supports API v5; IDS editors query the bSDD.
N21.err: Creating a custom Pset for something that already exists in a dictionary or in IFC.

N22.d: Table of elements by milestone with the required level in each cell and who is responsible. In the United States, Model Element Table; in other countries, progression matrix or LOIN matrix.
N22.ej: Structure 350 at detailed design, doors 300, furniture 100.
N22.eq: BEP spreadsheet or platforms such as Plannerly and BIMQ.

N23.d: Graphical setting in authoring tools (coarse/medium/fine, schematic/simplified/detailed) that decides which geometry is drawn at each scale. It is not a contractual level.
N23.eq: Revit: Detail Level (Coarse, Medium, Fine) per view; Archicad: Model View Options; Revit IFC exporter: “Level of Detail” = tessellation.
N23.err: Believing that a view set to “Fine” equals LOD 400.

N24.d: Native containers for alphanumerical information in each authoring tool. They should be defined once and with the name the requirement asks for.
N24.eq: Revit: shared parameters (TXT); Archicad: Property Manager and expressions; Allplan: attributes; Tekla: Trimble Connect property sets.
N24.err: Entering the data in a parameter that the IFC exporter does not map to any Pset.

N25.d: Platform that stores requirements by object, milestone, purpose and actor, and exports them to templates, rules or IDS.
N25.eq: dRofus, Plannerly, BIMQ, Cobuilder Require (exports one IDS per milestone and purpose).
N25.err: Managing hundreds of requirements in a spreadsheet with no version control.

N26.d: Grouping of properties of an IFC object. The standard buildingSMART Pset_ sets (e.g. Pset_DoorCommon) have fixed names and types; quantity sets (Qto_) store measurements.
N26.eq: Revit: Property Sets tab of the exporter and user-defined property set TXT files; Archicad: IFC Translators.
N26.err: Creating custom sets whose names start with “Pset_” or duplicating a standard property.

N27.d: buildingSMART standard (1.0, June 2024): an XML file with checkable requirements for an IFC, split into applicability and requirements, with six facets. Its header accepts purpose and milestone; it cannot require geometry.
N27.ej: Door IDS: FireRating with pattern “EI2? \d+(-C\d)?” and IsExternal as a boolean.
N27.eq: Import IDS: Archicad 28+, Allplan 2026, Vectorworks 2024+, BricsCAD V25; validate: IfcTester, Solibri (rule 244), BIMcollab Zoom; Revit with add-ins.
N27.err: Thinking IDS covers the whole level of information need: it leaves out geometry and documents.

N28.d: Subset of data for operation and maintenance (facilities, spaces, types, components, warranties). COBie v3 (2023) is part of NBIMS-US V4 and adds JSON.
N28.eq: COBie exporters in authoring tools; spreadsheets and IFC.
N28.err: Requesting full COBie at design stages.

N29.d: Method for describing the processes and information exchanges of a use case. ISO 29481-3:2022 provides a machine-readable data schema.
N29.eq: buildingSMART Use Case Management; IDS as the checkable technical part.
N29.err: Writing requirements without the process that justifies them.

N30.d: Verifying that a delivery meets its level of information need: that the properties exist, have a value and that the value is valid; geometry is reviewed with rules and sampling.
N30.ej: IfcTester 0.9.0: 1 of 3 doors passes the test IDS.
N30.eq: IfcTester, Solibri, BIMcollab Zoom, usBIM.IDS, xbim; the buildingSMART Validation Service does not check IDS.
N30.err: Checking only on receipt, when fixing is more expensive.

N31.d: Each country's documents that specify how to request levels of information: acronyms, scales, matrix templates and examples. Some follow the LOD 100-500 scale and others the level of information need.
N31.ej: Spain: UNE-EN ISO 7817-1:2025 and CBIM guides; Chile: MINVU NDI and Planbim; Peru: Plan BIM level of information need matrix; Germany: Arbeitshilfe LOIN-Konzept.
N31.err: Copying another country's matrix without adapting the purposes or milestones.

N32.d: Parts in preparation: Part 2 (ISO/DTS) is an application guide with examples and templates; Part 3 (ISO/DIS) defines a UML data model and an XSD schema for exchanging the level of information need.
N32.eq: Libraries that read drafts of Part 3 (e.g. openbim-loin).
N32.err: Implementing the Part 3 draft as if it were final.

G01.d: Integrated, data-driven virtual representation of real-world entities and processes, with synchronised interaction at a specified frequency and fidelity.
G01.ej: The Madrid City Council urban twin, which integrates 3D mapping and data from municipal sensors.
G01.eq: ISO/IEC 30173:2023 (standardised term); 'operational twin' in AWS IoT TwinMaker; 'twin graph' in Azure Digital Twins; 'facility twin' in Autodesk Tandem; 'iTwin' in Bentley; 'virtual twin' in Dassault.
G01.err: Calling any BIM model or 3D render a twin: without a data connection to the real asset there is no twin.

G02.d: Digital representation of a physical object with no automatic data exchange: any update between object and model is made manually (Kritzinger et al., 2018).
G02.ej: An as-built BIM model handed over at the end of construction and never updated after refurbishments.
G02.eq: Level 1 'Digital model' in Arup (2019); static asset information model (ISO 19650).
G02.err: Believing that an as-built BIM model is already a digital twin.

G03.d: Digital representation that receives data automatically from the physical object, but whose changes do not flow back to the object automatically (one-way flow) (Kritzinger et al., 2018).
G03.ej: A dashboard that shows room temperatures sent by the building management system (BMS) on a 3D model, without sending setpoints.
G03.eq: Many commercial operational 'digital twin' products work in practice as a digital shadow (monitoring without actuation).
G03.err: Thinking every twin must act on the asset: in construction most real cases are digital shadows, and it is legitimate to say so.

G04.d: Real item (building, bridge, equipment, network) that the twin represents and receives data from; ISO 55000 defines an asset as an item that has potential or actual value to an organisation.
G04.ej: A hospital chiller, a viaduct pier or a Canal de Isabel II pumping station.
G04.eq: IfcProduct/IfcElement in IFC; 'Asset' in AAS (IEC 63278); 'Equipment' in Brick; 'Entity' in AWS IoT TwinMaker.
G04.err: Confusing the asset with its model: the twin must identify each asset uniquely and stably.

G05.d: Scale that classifies a twin by its capability: Arup (2019) proposes 5 levels, from digital model to autonomous reasoning, assessing autonomy, intelligence, learning and fidelity.
G05.ej: A temperature alert system in a building would be level 2 (feedback and control) on the Arup scale.
G05.eq: Arup 1-5 (2019); ISO/IEC 30186:2025 'Digital twin — Maturity model and guidance for maturity assessment'.
G05.err: Treating maturity as a goal in itself: the right level depends on the use case, and is not always the highest.

G06.d: Ecosystem of digital twins connected through secure data sharing, proposed in the UK by the CDBB and now developed by the National Digital Twin Programme (NDTP).
G06.ej: UK programme that aims to connect water, energy and transport twins through a common information management framework.
G06.eq: CDBB Information Management Framework (IMF); Gemini Principles; NDTP Integration Architecture.
G06.err: Picturing it as a single giant model of the country: it is a federation of interoperable twins.

G07.d: Nine principles (CDBB, December 2018) for built-environment twins grouped into purpose, trust and function: public good, value creation, insight, security, openness, quality, federation, curation and evolution.
G07.ej: Using them as a checklist when drafting the tender specification for a twin of a public network.
G07.eq: Basis of the UK Information Management Framework; cited in ISO/IEC 30173 and AEC literature.
G07.err: Taking them as a technical standard: they are guiding principles, not verifiable requirements.

G08.d: Information model (geometry, data and documents) that supports asset management during operation, according to ISO 19650-1 and 19650-3.
G08.ej: A maintenance asset database populated with COBie when a public building is handed over.
G08.eq: ISO 19650-3:2020 (operational phase); 'Facility' in Autodesk Tandem; iModel in Bentley; AIM ≈ static layer of the twin.
G08.err: Confusing the AIM with the twin: the AIM is the reference database; the twin adds a live connection and analytics.

G09.d: Information model developed during design and construction (ISO 19650-2); at completion, the relevant part is transferred to the AIM.
G09.ej: Federated models of a hospital project managed in a CDE until handover.
G09.eq: ISO 19650-2:2018; information containers in the CDE.
G09.err: Handing over the full PIM as if it were the AIM, with construction data that is useless for operation.

G10.d: Owner's requirements on what asset information must be delivered for its management, derived from the organisational information requirements (OIR) according to ISO 19650.
G10.ej: List of mandatory attributes (manufacturer, serial number, warranty, maintenance interval) for each pump in a building.
G10.eq: ISO 19650-1/-3; can be expressed in a verifiable way with IDS (buildingSMART) or COBie templates.
G10.err: Writing generic AIR in a PDF that nobody can check automatically.

G13.d: Open buildingSMART schema for describing construction and infrastructure data; IFC 4.3 was published as ISO 16739-1:2024 (April 2024).
G13.ej: Exporting a viaduct model in IFC 4.3 with IfcBridge to load it into a twin platform.
G13.eq: Imported by Autodesk Tandem, Bentley iTwin (IFC connector), Nemetschek dTwin, Dalux; convertible to a graph (ifcOWL, Brick).
G13.err: Thinking IFC carries real-time sensor data: IFC describes the asset, not the telemetry stream.

G14.d: 128-bit globally unique identifier (encoded in 22 characters) of each IFC object; it allows an element to be traced from the model to the twin record.
G14.ej: Linking an air handling unit's maintenance tag to the GlobalId of the IfcUnitaryEquipment.
G14.eq: IfcRoot.GlobalId in IFC; 'externalId' in Autodesk Tandem; 'federationGuid' in iModel (⚠); mapping property in DTDL.
G14.err: Assuming the GUID is stable: some tools regenerate it on re-export, breaking traceability.

G15.d: IFC class (subtype of IfcDistributionControlElement) that represents a device measuring a physical quantity (temperature, flow, strain) and forming part of a control system.
G15.ej: A humidity sensor modelled in Revit and exported as IfcSensor with PredefinedType HUMIDITYSENSOR.
G15.err: Modelling the sensor only as generic geometry (IfcBuildingElementProxy), losing its semantics.

G16.d: IFC entities for recording an element's performance data over time (time series); rarely used in practice compared with time-series databases.
G16.ej: Storing a monthly summary of a pump's consumption in IFC when handing over the AIM.
G16.eq: IfcPerformanceHistory + IfcTimeSeries (IFC); time series in InfluxDB/Azure Data Explorer in practice.
G16.err: Trying to put high-frequency telemetry into IFC files.

G17.d: Exchange specification (usually a spreadsheet or IFC) with spaces, systems, components, types and documents for handover to maintenance; created by USACE in 2007.
G17.ej: Handing the owner a COBie workbook with all terminal units and their warranties.
G17.eq: NBIMS-US (COBie v3 in development, 2023 draft); BS 1192-4:2014 in the UK; COBie exporters in Revit, Archicad.
G17.err: Filling in COBie 'by hand' at the end of construction without linking it to the model GUIDs.

G18.d: buildingSMART standard (v1.0 approved on 4 June 2024) for defining information requirements in human-readable XML that can be checked automatically against IFC models.
G18.ej: An IDS file requiring every IfcPump to have 'Manufacturer' and 'SerialNumber' before it is loaded into the twin.
G18.eq: IfcTester (IfcOpenShell), Solibri, BIMcollab Zoom, usBIM.IDS and other validators; six facets: entity, attribute, property, classification, material, partOf.
G18.err: Confusing IDS with IFC: IDS describes which data are required, not the model.

G19.d: Open ontology (RDF/OWL) for describing equipment, points, spaces and system relationships in buildings (HVAC, lighting, meters) in a machine-readable way.
G19.ej: A Brick graph of a building in which a 'Supply_Air_Temperature_Sensor' feeds an 'AHU'.
G19.eq: brick:Equipment/Point/Location; alignments with Haystack, RealEstateCore and ASHRAE 223P; SHACL validation with the brickschema library.
G19.err: Using Brick for geometry: Brick describes system and point relationships, not shape or position.

G20.d: Open initiative for semantic tagging of building IoT data (tags such as 'ahu', 'temp', 'sensor'); Haystack 5 (2025) adds the Xeto schema language and RDF integration.
G20.ej: BMS points tagged 'discharge air temp sensor point' so that analytics can find them.
G20.eq: Haystack 4 (tags and defs); Haystack 5 with Xeto; used in SkySpark and many BMSs.
G20.err: Believing Haystack and Brick are locked in competition: they are converging through ASHRAE 223P.

G21.d: Open modular ontology (MIT licence) for real estate that links BIM/IFC, building control and IoT; basis of the DTDL building ontologies for Azure Digital Twins.
G21.ej: Modelling the spaces, floors and equipment of an office portfolio as REC twins in Azure Digital Twins.
G21.eq: REC in DTDL (Azure), WillowTwin (REC extension), RDF/OWL version.
G21.err: Thinking of it as an ISO standard: it is an open consortium that explicitly 'bridges' existing standards.

G22.d: W3C-OGC ontology (Recommendation, October 2017) for describing sensors, observations, procedures and actuators; SOSA is its lightweight core.
G22.ej: Describing that a strain gauge (sosa:Sensor) observes the deformation of a beam (sosa:FeatureOfInterest).
G22.eq: sosa:Sensor ≈ IfcSensor ≈ brick:Sensor; conceptual basis of SensorThings API.
G22.err: Using it to model the whole building: it focuses on observation and is combined with other ontologies.

G23.d: Open geospatial web API standard from OGC for interconnecting IoT devices, sensors and observations (Part 1 Sensing v1.0 2016, v1.1 2021; Part 2 Tasking).
G23.ej: Publishing a dam's piezometer readings as Thing/Datastream/Observation entities queryable via REST and MQTT.
G23.eq: Thing, Location, Datastream, Sensor, ObservedProperty, Observation and FeatureOfInterest entities; FROST-Server implementations.
G23.err: Confusing it with a low-level protocol: it defines a data model and an API, and uses HTTP/MQTT underneath.

G24.d: CityGML 3.0 module (OGC, 2021) that attaches time-varying values to city objects and links IoT sensors to the 3D city model.
G24.ej: Assigning hourly solar irradiation to a building façade, or linking a traffic sensor to a street segment.
G24.eq: CityGML 3.0 Dynamizer; can point to SensorThings API series.
G24.err: Thinking CityGML 3.0 replaces IFC: they work at different scales (city vs. building).

G25.d: Open Microsoft language based on JSON-LD for defining twin models (interfaces with properties, telemetry, relationships and components); versions v2, v3 and v4.
G25.ej: A 'Room' interface with a humidity property and a 'hasSensors' relationship, used for a university campus.
G25.eq: Azure Digital Twins (supports v2/v3), RealEstateCore and WillowTwin ontologies, Azure IoT Plug and Play.
G25.err: Believing DTDL is an ISO/IEC standard: it is an open Microsoft specification.

G26.d: Standardised digital representation (IEC 63278-1:2023) that gives uniform access to the information and services of an industrial asset through submodels.
G26.ej: A chiller's digital nameplate delivered by the manufacturer as an AAS.
G26.eq: IEC 63278; Industrie 4.0 / IDTA; Eclipse BaSyx; 'Digital Nameplate' and 'Technical Data' submodels.
G26.err: Considering it unrelated to construction: it is starting to be used for MEP equipment and products.

G27.d: Open format and API for describing and composing 3D scenes, originating at Pixar; the Alliance for OpenUSD published Core Specification 1.0 on 17 December 2025.
G27.ej: Composing a factory model in NVIDIA Omniverse from USD layers coming from Revit and from sensor data.
G27.eq: NVIDIA Omniverse; Autodesk and Bentley USD connectors; Cesium for Omniverse.
G27.err: Thinking USD replaces IFC: USD is scene/visualisation; IFC carries construction semantics.

G28.d: Open format created by Cesium (OGC Community Standard) for streaming large 3D datasets (cities, point clouds, BIM models) to the web in tiles.
G28.ej: Displaying in a browser a twin of a motorway with terrain, orthophoto and a tiled BIM model.
G28.eq: Cesium ion, CesiumJS, Cesium for Unreal/Unity/Omniverse, Bentley iTwin.
G28.err: Expecting full BIM semantics in 3D Tiles: it carries metadata, but its aim is efficient visualisation.

G29.d: Distributed database (built on SQLite) of the Bentley iTwin platform that aligns data from various engineering sources in a common schema and records changes ('changesets').
G29.ej: Synchronising IFC, DGN and Revit models of a metro line into a common iModel.
G29.eq: iTwin.js (open source); IFC/Revit/DGN connectors; BIS schemas (⚠ technical detail not verified in this session).
G29.err: Confusing an iModel with a file: it is a repository with a change history.

G30.d: Network of twins (nodes) connected by typed relationships (contains, feeds, serves) that allows the state of the system and its context to be queried.
G30.ej: Query: 'all rooms on level 3 served by AHU-2 with CO2 > 1000 ppm'.
G30.eq: Azure Digital Twins (twin graph), AWS IoT TwinMaker (knowledge graph), Brick RDF graph.
G30.err: Thinking the 3D model is the twin: the relationship graph usually adds more value than the geometry.

G31.d: Network of devices with sensors and connectivity that send data to computer systems; in a twin, it is the channel through which the asset's state is updated.
G31.ej: LoRaWAN occupancy sensors in the classrooms of a university building.
G31.eq: Azure IoT Hub, AWS IoT Core, Eclipse Ditto; standardised in ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 41.
G31.err: Thinking more sensors make a better twin: without a semantic model the data are hard to use.

G32.d: Lightweight publish/subscribe messaging protocol (OASIS; ISO/IEC 20922) widely used to send sensor telemetry to twin platforms.
G32.ej: A building gateway publishing 'building/l3/room12/co2' to a broker every minute.
G32.eq: Supported by Eclipse Ditto (MQTT 3.1.1 and 5), Azure IoT Hub, AWS IoT Core, SensorThings API.
G32.err: Believing MQTT provides semantics: it only carries messages; the meaning comes from the model (Brick, DTDL...).

G33.d: Industrial communication architecture (IEC 62541) with its own information model; a published mapping exists between BACnet (ISO 16484-5) and OPC UA.
G33.ej: Reading data from a water treatment plant (SCADA) into the network twin.
G33.eq: IEC 62541; companion specifications; OPC UA connectors in AWS IoT SiteWise, Azure IoT.
G33.err: Assuming OPC UA is industry-only: it appears in infrastructure and large facilities.

G34.d: Communication protocol for building automation and control (ASHRAE 135 / ISO 16484-5), a common source of operational HVAC and lighting data.
G34.ej: Integrating the BACnet points of a hospital BMS into Autodesk Tandem or Willow through a connector.
G34.eq: ISO 16484-5; mapping to OPC UA; points can be tagged with Haystack/Brick.
G34.err: Thinking BACnet point names are self-explanatory: they are usually codes that need mapping.

G35.d: Strategy that anticipates failures from condition data and analytical models in order to intervene before a breakdown; level 3 on the Arup scale.
G35.ej: Detecting from vibration and power consumption that a booster pump is degrading, and scheduling its replacement.
G35.eq: AWS IoT TwinMaker + SiteWise; Azure Digital Twins + analytics; Autodesk Tandem (threshold alerts).

G36.d: Continuous measurement (strain, vibration, tilt, temperature) of a structure's behaviour to detect damage and support maintenance decisions.
G36.ej: The monitoring system of the Queensferry Crossing bridge (Scotland), with hundreds of sensors.
G36.eq: Bentley iTwin IoT / SHM partners; SensorThings for publication; IfcSensor for modelling sensors.
G36.err: Calling an SHM system a twin when there is no associated bridge model: it is monitoring, not necessarily a twin.

G37.d: Time between a change in the asset and its reflection in the twin, and the update rate; the DTC definition requires a frequency specified according to the use case.
G37.ej: Room occupancy: every 5 min is enough; bridge vibration: sampling at hundreds of Hz with aggregation.
G37.eq: Design parameter in any platform (IoT Hub, SiteWise, Tandem streams).
G37.err: Demanding 'real time' for everything, raising cost without adding value.

G38.d: Progressive deviation of a sensor's reading from the true value; periodic calibration and anomaly detection are part of the twin's quality control.
G38.ej: A CO2 probe that after two years reads 150 ppm too high and triggers ventilation unnecessarily.
G38.eq: Calibration metadata in SSN/SOSA (procedure), Brick (properties), maintenance records.
G38.err: Trusting the data because 'it comes from the sensor' without a calibration plan.

G39.d: W3C language for validating RDF graphs against 'shapes' (constraints); used to check that a Brick model conforms to the ontology.
G39.ej: Validating with the brickschema Python library that every sensor has 'isPointOf' to a piece of equipment.
G39.eq: brickschema (Python), pySHACL, TopBraid; ASHRAE 223P is also defined with SHACL.
G39.err: Validating only RDF syntax and not semantic consistency.

G40.d: Formal model of the concepts and relationships of a domain that allows different systems to interpret the twin's data in the same way.
G40.ej: Using Brick + IFC + SOSA so that analytics, maintenance and BIM all talk about the same 'equipment'.
G40.eq: Brick, RealEstateCore, ifcOWL, SSN/SOSA, ASHRAE 223P; DTDL as a modelling language.
G40.err: Inventing a bespoke ontology for every project instead of extending an existing one.

G41.d: Structured delivery of the project information (PIM) to the owner to form the AIM and feed the twin, verifying the agreed requirements.
G41.ej: Crossrail handed over the Elizabeth line asset information to TfL as part of handover.
G41.err: Leaving handover until the end: information must be accumulated and validated throughout construction.

G42.d: City-scale twin that integrates a 3D model, geospatial data, sensors and simulations for urban planning and management.
G42.ej: Virtual Singapore (NRF, since 2014) or the Madrid City Council digital twin.
G42.err: Equating a 3D city viewer with a twin that has no live data or simulation.

G43.d: Degree of detail and accuracy with which the twin reproduces the asset (geometry, data and behaviour); it should be sufficient for the use case.
G43.ej: Managing occupancy only needs a space model; SHM needs a calibrated structural model.
G43.eq: Arup 'Fidelity' metric; 'fidelity' in the DTC definition; level of information need (ISO 7817-1).
G43.err: Chasing maximum geometric fidelity when the value lies in the data.

D01.d: Incompatibility between elements of one or more models (spatial, clearance or time-based) that would prevent building, operating or maintaining the asset as designed; it is detected by comparing sets of elements against agreed rules and tolerances.
D01.ej: An HVAC duct runs through a concrete beam.
D01.eq: Navisworks: Clash; Solibri: Issue/Clash (component intersection rule); Revit: Interference Check; ACC Model Coordination: Clash; IfcClash: clash; BCF: Topic (type Clash)
D01.err: Mistaking a geometric result for a real problem: many results are irrelevant or duplicated.

D02.d: Two elements occupy the same physical space: their geometries intersect beyond the accepted penetration tolerance.
D02.ej: A drainage pipe passing through a column.
D02.eq: Navisworks: Hard / Hard (Conservative); Solibri: Intersection; ACC: Hard clash; IfcClash: intersection/collision
D02.err: Reporting planned penetrations (sleeves) or tangential contacts without tolerance as hard clashes.

D03.d: An element intrudes into the minimum distance or free volume required around another (insulation, installation, access, safety) even though it does not touch it.
D03.ej: A cable tray 5 cm from a duct where 30 cm of separation is required.
D03.eq: Navisworks: Clearance; Solibri: Clearance / distance rule; Revizto: Clearance (with H/V offsets); IfcClash: clearance
D03.err: Applying a single clearance to the whole model; clearance depends on the system and should be modelled as a volume when it is for maintenance.

D04.d: Conflict that arises when the model is linked to the schedule: two activities, crews or workspaces coincide in place and time, or the sequence makes it impossible to install something.
D04.ej: The crane's slewing radius encroaches on the façade installation zone in week 32.
D04.eq: Navisworks: Clash Detective with TimeLiner; Synchro: 4D conflicts; ACC/Revizto: limited
D04.err: Treating it with the same rules as a static spatial clash.

D05.d: Numerical value that defines what gets reported: for hard clashes, the minimum penetration from which a clash is reported; for clearance, the maximum distance below which it is reported. It is usually adjusted by stage and discipline.
D05.ej: Hard with 10 mm to ignore modelling contacts; 50 mm clearance between ducts.
D05.eq: Navisworks: Tolerance; Solibri: tolerance in rules; Revizto: Tolerance; IfcClash: tolerance/clearance
D05.err: Confusing detection tolerance with construction tolerance, or raising it so far that it hides real clashes.

D06.d: Table, agreed in the BEP, that defines which pairs of disciplines or systems are checked, with which type of test and tolerance, at which stage, with which priority and who is responsible.
D06.ej: ARC vs STR hard 0 mm; DRN vs HVAC clearance 25 mm; ELE vs all, construction stage.
D06.eq: Navisworks: list of Tests; Solibri: Ruleset; ACC: Clash test (automatic); BIMcollab/Revizto: Clash sets
D06.err: Testing 'everything against everything' without a matrix and getting thousands of useless results.

D07.d: Bringing together results with a common cause or solution (same element, system, level, zone or person responsible) to manage them as a single issue.
D07.ej: 40 clashes between the same cable tray and 40 joists are handled as one issue.
D07.eq: Navisworks: Clash groups/Group; Solibri: grouping of results into Issues; BIM Track: Clash grouper; Revizto: Grouping; IfcClash: smart grouping
D07.err: Grouping only by level or grid, mixing problems that belong to different people.

D08.d: Result that the tool flags as a clash but needs no action: an intentional contact, an element not modelled in enough detail, a problem that can be solved on site or an element already resolved.
D08.ej: A clash between pipe insulation and its clamp.
D08.eq: Navisworks: Approved/Resolved; Solibri: Accepted/Rejected; ACC: Not an issue; BCF: closed TopicStatus
D08.err: Approving in bulk without criteria or, conversely, sending everything to the disciplines.

D09.d: Process of bringing together each discipline's models, without merging them or losing their authorship, into a georeferenced federated model on which incompatibilities are detected and resolved.
D09.ej: Architecture, structure and MEP in IFC federated in a common viewer with a shared origin.
D09.eq: Navisworks: NWF/NWD; Solibri: SMC with several IFC files; ACC: Coordination space; Revizto/BIMcollab Zoom; Trimble Connect
D09.err: Federating models with different origins or versions, or coordinating on a 'merged' model that erases authorship.

D10.d: Manageable record of a detected problem, with title, description, type, status, priority, assignee, due date, comments and associated views; in BCF it is called a Topic.
D10.ej: Topic 'Duct C-12 against beam V-3, level 2', assigned to MEP, due Friday.
D10.eq: BCF: Topic; Navisworks: Clash result/Issue; Solibri: Issue; ACC: Issue; Revizto: Issue; Trimble Connect: ToDo
D10.err: Using the issue as a screenshot with no assignee or status.

D11.d: Display state associated with an issue: camera (orthogonal or perspective), clipping planes, selected, visible or coloured components (by IFC GUID) and a reference image.
D11.ej: viewpoint.bcfv with camera, two components selected by IfcGuid and snapshot.png.
D11.eq: BCF: .bcfv + PNG/JPEG snapshot; Navisworks: Viewpoint; Solibri: Slide; ACC/Revizto: issue view
D11.err: Sharing only the image without components: the recipient cannot select the elements in their own software.

D12.d: Repeated or overlapping elements with identical (or nearly identical) geometry in the same place, within one model or across models; they inflate quantities and clash results.
D12.ej: A column modelled in both architecture and structure, or a wall copied twice.
D12.eq: Navisworks: Duplicates; Solibri: duplicate components rule; Revit: 'identical instances' warning
D12.err: Not running it before cross-discipline tests, multiplying the results.

D13.t: Clash resolution hierarchy / right of way
D13.d: Order, agreed in the BEP, that decides which system gives way in a clash according to its flexibility: larger, permanent or constrained elements (structure, gravity drainage) take priority.
D13.ej: Gravity drainage > ducts > pressurised pipes/fire protection > cable trays and electrical conduits.
D13.eq: BEP priority matrix; ETS: severity A/B/C; Ashghal: priority A-C and severity 1-4
D13.err: Applying it without exceptions (e.g. a small duct against a main sewer).

D14.d: Open buildingSMART standard for exchanging issues about models (IFC or others) without sending the model: XML (BCF-XML, .bcfzip/.bcf container) or web services (BCF API). Versions 1.0 (2011), 2.0, 2.1 and 3.0.
D14.ej: Exporting 25 topics from Solibri in BCF 2.1 and importing them into Revit with BCF Manager.
D14.eq: BCF-XML 2.1/3.0; BCF API 2.1/3.0; add-ins for Revit/Archicad/Tekla; BIMcollab; Revizto; Trimble Connect; Catenda; Bonsai
D14.err: Mixing versions (3.0 vs 2.1) or losing fields (priority, server id) on export.

D15.d: REST/JSON specification for synchronising BCF issues between applications and servers; it belongs to the OpenCDE family together with the Foundation API (discovery, OAuth 2.0, user) and the Documents API (download/upload to the CDE).
D15.ej: A Revit add-in calls GET /bcf/3.0/projects/{id}/topics and updates the status without passing files around.
D15.eq: BCF API 2.1/3.0; OpenCDE Foundation API 1.0/1.1; Documents API 1.0
D15.err: Assuming that 'supports BCF' means supporting the API (many tools only read/write files).

D16.d: Information management framework (EN ISO 19650) that allocates coordination: each task team reviews and coordinates its information before sharing it; the lead appointed party defines the federation strategy, the container breakdown structure and the responsibility matrix, and compiles the TIDPs into the MIDP.
D16.ej: The BEP sets the federation strategy by building and discipline, and the matrix that assigns clash detection to the delivery team's coordinator.
D16.eq: ISO 19650-1/-2 (2018; 2026 revision); UNE-EN ISO 19650; UK BIM Framework; Plan BIM (Orden PCM/818/2023)
D16.err: Believing that ISO 19650 defines job titles (BIM Manager) or the clash detection procedure: it defines functions and processes.

D17.d: Unique 128-bit identifier of each IFC object, encoded in 22 characters (alphabet 0-9A-Za-z_$); BCF uses it (IfcGuid) to reference components, so it must remain stable between exports.
D17.ej: 2O2Fr$t4X7Zf8NOew3FLOH identifies the same door in every version of the IFC file.
D17.eq: IFC: GlobalId; BCF: IfcGuid; Revit: IfcGUID/IFC GUID parameter (derived from the UniqueId); Archicad: IFC GlobalId; Tekla: GUID
D17.err: Regenerating GUIDs on export (copy/paste, delete and redraw) breaks issue traceability.

D18.d: Saved grouping of elements of the federated model used as side A or B of a clash test. A selection set stores specific elements (static); a search set stores criteria (property, category, system) and is re-evaluated when the model changes (dynamic).
D18.ej: Search set 'MEP – Drainage' = elements whose 'System Type' contains 'Sanitary'; it is tested against the search set 'STR – Beams'. When the new model version is loaded, the set automatically includes the new pipes.
D18.eq: Navisworks: Selection Set / Search Set (Sets window, Find Items); BIMcollab Zoom: Smart Views as source/target set; Revizto: search sets A/B; Solibri: rule component filters; Archicad: Group 1 / Group 2 by criteria; IfcClash: group A/B selectors; MicroStation: levels/references/Named Groups.
D18.err: Using static selection sets in repeated tests: new elements from the next delivery are left out and the test gives a false 'zero clashes'. Also: criteria based on non-standardised names.

D19.t: Clash rules / ignore rules and rulesets
D19.d: Conditions that stop the program from reporting certain clashes (ignore rules) and saved, reusable groupings of checking rules (rulesets). They remove systematic false positives and standardise checking.
D19.ej: In Navisworks, enabling 'Items in Same File' to skip clashes within each discipline and the 'Insulation Thickness' template for insulated pipes; in Solibri, an 'MEP-STR Coordination' ruleset with the General Intersection Rule and 'duct passes through wall' exceptions.
D19.eq: Navisworks: Rules tab (6 default rules + templates); Solibri: Ruleset / Intersection Exceptions; Revizto: Ignore rules; Bentley: Suppression rules; Trimble Connect: 'Ignore clashes within the same file/type'; Archicad: 'Participates in Collision Detection' by material; BIMcollab Zoom: Local/Shared rulesets.
D19.err: Rules that are too broad (e.g. 'Same File' on a model federated into a single NWD) that hide real clashes; or not documenting the rules in the BEP, so each coordinator gets different results.

D20.d: Volume that must be kept free around equipment or elements in order to operate, maintain, replace or access them safely; it is modelled as an auxiliary solid and checked with clearance or hard tests against that volume.
D20.ej: A 1 m zone in front of an electrical panel, or the access-panel opening zone of an AHU.
D20.eq: 'Clearance' families/objects in Revit; Solibri: free space rule; Navisworks: test against clearance solids
D20.err: Not modelling it and relying on the global tolerance; or modelling it as a solid that is then measured or exported as a real element.

D21.d: Clash calculation run by a service in the CDE without manual intervention when a model is published or updated in a coordination space, or on a schedule, leaving the results accessible to the whole team.
D21.ej: When the new version of the HVAC IFC file is uploaded to the coordination space, Forma Model Coordination recalculates the clashes against structure and architecture and shows them grouped.
D21.eq: Model Coordination (Autodesk Forma/BIM Collaborate Pro), Clash Automation (Revizto), clash spaces (Aconex), cloud clash sets (Trimble Connect).
D21.err: Assuming that 'automated' means as configurable as Navisworks: Model Coordination has no tolerance or test matrix in the calculation, only filters afterwards; or leaving container models switched on and multiplying noise and processing time.

D22.d: Sequence of statuses an issue goes through from creation until its closure is verified (e.g. New → Active/Assigned → Resolved by the author → Verified/Closed, or Dismissed), with assignee, dates and history.
D22.ej: The coordinator creates the issue 'Duct vs beam L3' (Open) and assigns it to MEP; MEP marks it Resolved; after re-running the test the coordinator moves it to Closed.
D22.err: Mapping statuses incorrectly between programs: BCF does not fix values, each server defines them in extensions; on import into ACC everything arrives as 'Open' except 'Closed'; confusing 'Resolved' with 'Closed'.

D23.d: Metrics that measure the health of the coordination process: open/closed issues, new issues per cycle, mean time to close, age, reopened issues, trend by discipline or zone and the identified/resolved ratio.
D23.ej: Weekly dashboard: 42 open (−15 %), mean time to close 9 days, 6 reopened; MEP-structure accounts for 60 % of the open issues on L2.
D23.eq: Clash metrics, coordination dashboard, clash aging.
D23.err: Measuring the raw number of clashes (dominated by false positives and duplicates) instead of grouped issues; comparing cycles with different tests or tolerances.

D24.d: Regular session (usually weekly or fortnightly) around the federated model in which prioritised issue groups are reviewed, solutions are agreed and owners and deadlines are assigned, recorded in BCF/CDE.
D24.ej: Weekly meeting: review of 15 priority issues on level 3 with MEP and structure.
D24.eq: ACC/BIM 360 Coordination; Revizto; BIMcollab; Navisworks in the meeting room; Teams + BCF
D24.err: Reviewing clash by clash without preparation and without assigning tasks at the end.

D25.d: Degree of geometric and alphanumeric development each element must have for a purpose; coordination needs geometry with size, position and interfaces (e.g. BIMForum LOD 350), defined according to the LOIN (EN ISO 7817-1:2024).
D25.ej: Ducts with insulation and supports modelled before trade coordination.
D25.eq: BIMForum LOD 100-500 (350 for coordination); EN ISO 7817-1 (LOIN); IDS to check requirements
D25.err: Running clash detection on LOD 200 models and making decisions on generic geometry.

D26.d: Check that an issue marked as resolved really is: the same test (same rules and tolerance) is re-run on the new version of the models and it is confirmed that the clash disappears without creating others, before the issue is closed.
D26.ej: After the new version of the plumbing model, the coordinator re-runs the PLU_v_STR test; the clash disappears and the issue moves from Resolved to Closed; a new clash with the suspended ceiling generates another issue.
D26.eq: Re-run, verify fix, Approved/Resolved in Clash Detective, clashes shown in red as out of date (Trimble Connect).
D26.err: Closing on the author's word without re-running, or re-running with a different tolerance or model and accepting the disappearance as valid.

P01.d: Plan explaining how the delivery team will manage and deliver the information for an appointment to meet the EIR: people, strategy, federation, responsibilities, methods, standard and resources.
P01.ej: The Andalusian regional government (AOPJA) calls it PEB and asks for a pre-PEB with the tender and the PEB after award.
P01.eq: ISO 19650-2: BIM execution plan; Penn State: BIM Project Execution Plan (PxP); NBIMS-US V4: BIM Execution Plan; ISO revision in progress: possibly «Information Production Plan».
P01.err: Writing a generic company manual that answers no specific requirement of the EIR.

P02.d: Version of the BEP that each prospective lead appointed party submits with its tender (ISO 19650-2, 5.3.2) to show how it will meet the EIR; it includes a high-level responsibility matrix.
P02.ej: pre-PEB in the AOPJA model EIR (2024).
P02.eq: PAS 1192-2: pre-contract BEP; Penn State: proposal.
P02.err: Presenting it as a sales brochure instead of a point-by-point response to the EIR.

P03.d: BEP that the appointed delivery team confirms and details after the appointment (ISO 19650-2, 5.4.1): names of the people, detailed matrix, agreed methods and standard. It forms part of the contract documents.
P03.ej: PEB after award in the AOPJA tender documents.
P03.err: Not updating it after signing: halfway through the project it describes a team that no longer exists.

P04.d: Information requirements for a specific appointment (management, commercial and technical aspects). The appointing party writes them and the lead appointed party passes them on to each appointed party.
P04.ej: «BIM Requirements (EIR)» annex of the AOPJA tender documents.
P04.eq: PAS 1192-2: Employer's Information Requirements; Spanish BIM Plan: BIM requirements in the technical specifications.
P04.err: Still reading EIR as «Employer's»: under ISO 19650 there is an EIR for every appointment, including those to subcontractors.

P05.d: Information requirements linked to the organization's strategic objectives for its assets; they feed the PIR and the AIR.
P05.ej: A city council that needs to know the energy consumption of all its buildings.
P05.err: Skipping them and writing the EIR without knowing which decisions the information is for.

P06.d: Requirements relating to the purpose, design and construction of the asset, linked to the project's key decision points; they determine the project information model (PIM).
P06.ej: Information to decide whether to tender the works at the end of the detailed design.
P06.err: Confusing them with the EIR: the PIR belongs to the project; the EIR, to each appointment.

P07.d: Requirements for the information needed to operate and maintain the asset; they determine the content of the asset information model (AIM).
P07.ej: Maintenance data for HVAC equipment requested by the facility manager.
P07.eq: ISO 19650-1 and -3; COBie as the usual format.
P07.err: Asking for them at the end of construction instead of including them from the first EIR.

P08.d: Information model (structured and unstructured containers) developed during the delivery phase that transfers to the AIM what the AIR requires.
P08.ej: Models, drawings and documents for the design and construction of a hospital.
P08.err: Thinking it is only the federated 3D model.

P09.d: Information model of the operational phase; it receives the relevant information from the PIM at project close-out.
P09.ej: Maintenance database of the handed-over building.
P09.err: Handing over the whole PIM as the AIM without filtering what is actually useful for operation.

P10.d: Receiver of information concerning works, goods or services: usually the client or whoever manages information on its behalf. It writes the EIR and accepts the information.
P10.ej: A ministry or a public works agency tendering a project.
P10.err: Simply calling it «the client» when in fact a delegated information manager is acting.

P11.d: Party appointed by the appointing party that coordinates and manages information between its delivery team and the appointing party. It writes the BEP and the MIDP.
P11.ej: The architecture practice that wins the competition and subcontracts structures and building services.
P11.err: Assuming there is only one per project: there is one for every delivery team.

P12.d: Provider of information appointed by the lead appointed party; it receives its own EIR and writes the TIDP for its task teams.
P12.ej: The structural engineering firm subcontracted by the architecture practice.
P12.err: Not passing it its own EIR: it then does not know what it must deliver.

P13.d: Group made up of a lead appointed party and its appointed parties.
P13.ej: Architecture + structures + building services under one main contract.
P13.eq: ISO 19650: delivery team. In Spanish also «equipo de ejecución» (UNE translation to be confirmed).
P13.err: Confusing it with the project team, which also includes the appointing party and other delivery teams.

P14.d: Group of people carrying out a specific package of work within an appointed party.
P14.ej: The electrical services team within the engineering firm.
P14.err: Treating the whole company as a single task team and losing the detail of the TIDP.

P15.d: The appointing party plus all the project's delivery teams.
P15.ej: Developer, design team and contractor of the same project.

P16.d: Table assigning who produces each piece of information: high-level in the pre-appointment BEP and detailed (by container, milestone and responsible party) after the appointment.
P16.ej: Spreadsheet with containers in rows and teams in columns.
P16.eq: ISO 19650-2: high-level / detailed responsibility matrix; RACI in project management.
P16.err: Rows with two «responsible» parties: if everyone is responsible, no one is.

P17.d: List of the containers each task team will deliver, with level of information need, format, date and responsible party.
P17.ej: TIDP of the structures team for the scheme design.
P17.err: Doing it once and not updating it when the programme changes.

P18.d: Plan bringing together the TIDPs of the whole delivery team, aligned with the appointing party's information delivery milestones.
P18.ej: MIDP of the team that won a hospital competition.
P18.eq: ISO 19650-2; Peru: «programa general de desarrollo de la información» (UNE translation to be confirmed).
P18.err: Using it as a construction Gantt chart instead of as an information plan.

P19.d: Point at which the appointing party needs information to make a decision; it may fall at the end of a stage or within it.
P19.ej: Delivery before applying for the building permit.
P19.err: Setting milestones for the team's convenience rather than around the client's decisions.

P20.d: How information is split into containers (by discipline, volume, level…) and how they are brought together for coordination.
P20.ej: One model per discipline and building, federated every week.
P20.eq: ISO 19650-2 (pre-appointment BEP); information container breakdown structure.
P20.err: Splitting the model according to each program's habits without thinking about who produces it.

P21.d: Common rules for information: naming, classification, units, levels of information need, coordinate reference system and formats. The BEP proposes changes and the post-appointment BEP fixes them.
P21.ej: Naming convention + metres + EPSG:25830 + Alicante heights.
P21.err: Leaving coordinates out: each discipline picks its own origin.

P22.d: How information is produced, checked, reviewed, approved and shared on the project.
P22.ej: Internal review before moving a file to shared.
P22.err: Confusing them with the standard: the standard says what information looks like; the methods, how the work is done.

P23.d: Contractual annex that brings information management into the appointment: responsibilities, licences and use of the information.
P23.err: Signing the contract without it: the BEP then binds no one.

P24.d: Named persistent set of information retrievable from a file system or application: a drawing, a model, a schedule, a document.
P24.err: Thinking only of models: a PDF or a spreadsheet is a container too.

P25.d: Status of each container in the common data environment: work in progress, shared, published and archived. Each transition requires a check, review or authorization.
P25.ej: A WIP folder for each team and a published folder for the project.
P25.eq: ISO 19650-1; Autodesk Docs and BCDE Project implement them with statuses and workflows.
P25.err: Having the four folders with no one signing off the transitions.

P26.d: Metadata indicating what a container is suitable for: S0 work in progress; S1–S7 shared; A, B and CR published (2021 UK National Annex).
P26.ej: S1 suitable for coordination; A1 authorized and accepted.
P26.eq: BS EN ISO 19650-2 NA; Autodesk Docs (attribute); other CDEs with their own lists.
P26.err: Using S for «unchecked» and A for «approved» without defining the list in the project's information standard.

P27.d: Version identifier of the container: P01, P02… preliminary; C01, C02… contractual; P01.01 for interim versions.
P27.ej: P03 in shared; C01 on publishing.
P27.err: Restarting the numbering when the state changes.

P28.d: Rule for identifying containers by fields separated by hyphens: project-originator-volume-level-type-role-number (UK National Annex).
P28.eq: BS EN ISO 19650-2 NA; Autodesk Docs naming standard validator.
P28.err: Copying the UK convention without defining the codes of each field for the project.

P29.d: How the team will set up and test resources, technology and methods before producing information (ISO 19650-2, 5.3.5 and 5.5).
P29.ej: IFC export test and upload to the CDE in the first week.
P29.err: Starting production without having tested the whole workflow.

P30.d: The eight ISO 19650-2 activities for each appointment: assessment and need, invitation to tender, tender response, appointment, mobilization, collaborative production of information, information model delivery and project close-out.
P30.eq: ISO 19650-2, clause 5; ISO 19650-3 for the operational phase.
P30.err: Reading the BEP as a standalone document rather than as part of that process.

P31.d: International standards for information management using BIM: 1 concepts, 2 delivery phase, 3 operational phase, 4 information exchange, 5 security, 6 health and safety. In Spain, UNE-EN ISO 19650.
P31.err: Citing «ISO 19650» without the part: the BEP is in part 2.

P32.d: Specific ways of applying BIM to achieve an objective (3D coordination, quantity take-off, simulation…); the backbone of the Penn State guide and NBIMS-US.
P32.ej: 3D coordination and drawing extraction, required at the Initial level of the Spanish BIM Plan.
P32.eq: Penn State BIM PxP Guide; NBIMS-US V4; Spanish BIM Plan.
P32.err: Asking for «all uses» in the EIR without saying which decision each one serves.

P33.t: Spanish BIM plan for public procurement (Plan BIM)
P33.d: Plan for the Incorporation of the BIM Methodology in public procurement (Council of Ministers Agreement of 27/06/2023, Order PCM/818/2023): timetable of BIM levels required by contract value.
